gaps.sentence: She ___ very well in her end-of-year exams.
gaps.hint: collocation: to ___ well in an exam
gaps.explanation: do well in an exam is the standard phrase meaning to perform successfully.

gaps.sentence: Her company ___ a huge profit last year.
gaps.explanation: make a profit (or make a loss) is the fixed business collocation.

gaps.sentence: He was so badly ___ in the fall that he needed an operation.
gaps.explanation: badly hurt is the standard collocation meaning seriously injured.

gaps.sentence: We ___ to the conclusion that the project was not viable.
gaps.explanation: come to the conclusion that ... is the fixed phrase; 'reach' and 'arrive' do not take 'to'.

gaps.sentence: She has a ___ Scottish accent that is hard to miss.
gaps.explanation: a strong accent is the standard collocation; 'heavy accent' and 'deep accent' are not used.

gaps.sentence: The storm ___ a lot of damage to the roof.
gaps.explanation: do damage to something is the collocation; past tense 'did' is needed here.

gaps.sentence: Over five hundred athletes will ___ part in the games.
gaps.explanation: take part in something means to participate in it.

gaps.sentence: Grandad's best man ___ a joke that made everyone laugh.
gaps.explanation: tell a joke is the fixed collocation; 'say a joke' is not used.
